_README: Where Harry actually stands right now. Used by the follow-up nudges to add
ONE true sentence about his timeline - nothing else reads this file.
Why it exists: an offer in hand is the strongest thing a candidate can say
to a live conversation, and it is also the easiest thing in the world to
overstate. So it is written down as facts with an expiry rather than left
to a model to phrase, and every rule below is enforced in code:
- The offering employer is NEVER named. It is nobody else's business, and
in a small market it would get back to the recruiter who placed him.
- It says an offer exists. It never says what it is worth, never invents a
competing bid, and never implies another employer has offered more.
- decide_by is a hard expiry. Past that date the sentence disappears on its
own, because 'I have an offer' stops being true the moment he accepts or
declines one and a stale claim is a lie he did not choose to tell.
- It is only ever added to a FOLLOW-UP, never to a first approach. Leading
with leverage to somebody who has not met you reads as arrogance.
Set offer to null the moment it is accepted or declined.

offer.note: Offer received via a recruiter for a technician role in Aberdeen. Employer deliberately not recorded - it is never named in an email.

interview_booked.note: Second interview booked with another Aberdeen employer for Friday 21 August.
